transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I guess the main thing is that I just stopped caring about everything. Things I used to look forward to just don't matter anymore. My fishing gear is still sitting untouched in the garage from last season. Going out to the woodshop just feels like a chore now, so I don't even bother. And even when my kids try to get me to play chess with them, I’m just going through the motions. I just don't have any interest in it.
When did you first notice that you stopped caring about these things? Was it a gradual change over weeks or months, or did it happen more suddenly?

It's been a while now. I'd say... about a year and seven months. It didn't really just fade out slowly out of nowhere. It was more tied to... well, it started right around the time my wife’s health problems began. That just changed everything at home, and since then, I just haven't had it in me to care about much else.
Besides losing interest in your hobbies, how has your mood been overall during this past year and a half? Would you say you've been feeling sad, empty, or down most days?

I don't really know how to describe it, honestly. I wouldn't say I feel sad, exactly. It's more like... I just feel empty. Like there's nothing there. Most days I just feel flat and worn out, and it's been like that pretty consistently since all this started.

In the past year and a half since your wife's health problems started, have there been any periods where you felt somewhat better or more like yourself, even if just for a few weeks or a couple months? Or has this empty, flat feeling been pretty constant the whole time?
No, not really. It's just been a constant thing. I haven't had any breaks from it where I felt better or anything. It's just been that same empty feeling every day since it all started.

You mentioned the empty, flat feeling has been constant since your wife's health problems started. But I want to make sure I understand—during these past 18 months, have there been any stretches of time, even just a month or two, where you felt noticeably better or had more energy and interest in things?

Like I said... no, not at all. There hasn't been a month, or even a couple of weeks, where things lifted. I haven't had any stretches where my energy came back or I felt like myself again. It really has just been a flat line this entire time. No breaks.

Before your wife's health problems started about 18 months ago, have you ever experienced periods in your life where you felt this same kind of emptiness and loss of interest for weeks or months at a time?

No, I don't think so. I mean, life has its normal ups and downs, stressful days on the job and all that, but... nothing like this. Before she got sick, I was fine. I never felt this kind of constant emptiness or just... stopped caring about things for months on end. This is completely new for me.

When your wife's health problems first started 18 months ago, do you remember how you felt emotionally in those first few weeks? Did the empty, flat feeling come on right away, or did it develop gradually over time after the initial shock?

It came on pretty much right away. I mean, there was the initial shock of it all, sure, but then everything just... went flat. So, yeah, this has been going on for about a year and seven months now, basically ever since my wife's health problems changed everything at home.

You've mentioned this empty, flat feeling has been going on for about 18 months now. But I want to make sure I have the timeline right—when your wife first got sick, did you start feeling this way within the first couple of weeks, or did it take longer than that for the emptiness to really set in?

Like I just mentioned... yeah, it was within those first couple of weeks. It really didn't take long at all to set in. Once that initial shock kind of settled, the emptiness just took over, and I've been stuck like this ever since.

You mentioned your wife's health problems started about 18 months ago, and the emptiness came on within a couple of weeks after that. But before her health problems began, in the weeks or months leading up to that event, did you notice any of these empty or flat feelings starting to develop?

No, not at all. Like I said before, everything was fine until she got sick. There was no... build-up or anything like that in the weeks before it happened. I was just going to work, living normal life. The empty feeling didn't start until after we got the news.

You said the emptiness came on within a couple of weeks after your wife got sick. Just to be precise—did you start feeling this empty, flat way within the first 2 weeks, or was it more like 3 to 4 weeks after you got the news before it really took hold?

It was definitely within those first two weeks. I mean, I wasn't exactly counting the days back then, but it was fast. Like I've been saying, this has been going on for about a year and seven months now, basically ever since her health problems changed everything at home. So, yeah, it was right at the start of all that. It definitely didn't take a whole month to set in.

You mentioned your wife's health problems started about 18 months ago. Just to clarify the exact timing—roughly how many weeks or months after you first learned about her health problems did the empty, flat feeling actually begin?

I feel like we're going in circles a bit here. Like I just said a second ago, it was within those first two weeks. I can't give you an exact number of days, but it was right after we got the news. It definitely wasn't months later.

During these 18 months of feeling empty and flat, have there been any individual days—even just one or two days here and there—where you felt noticeably better or more like yourself, or has it truly been every single day with no breaks at all?
No... no breaks. It's been every single day. I mean, I haven't had a day where I felt better or, you know, like my old self. It's just... always there. Every day is exactly the same.
During these past 18 months, has there been any stretch of time—say 2 months or longer—where you felt completely back to normal with no empty or flat feelings at all?
No, definitely not. Like I just said, it's been every single day. There hasn't been a single day where I felt normal, let alone a whole two months. It's just been a constant thing this whole time.

I want to make absolutely sure about this—in the entire 18 months since your wife got sick, has there been even one stretch of 2 months or longer where you felt completely back to normal with no empty or flat feelings at all, or has it truly been constant with no breaks whatsoever?

I feel like we're just repeating the same question over and over now. Like I just said, no. There hasn't been a two-month break. There hasn't even been a one-day break. It's been constant, every single day, for the whole 18 months. No breaks at all.
